channel.title: Ayiti Sitwayen · Candidates under scrutiny
channel.description: Understand the record, follow the money and examine documented connections. Each article follows one question in plain language.

item.title: After Jude Elie’s migrant-rights appeal, a court record that needs its correction
item.description: An April 2026 order explains why a March ruling cannot be summarised as dismissing the whole of Count 4.

item.title: Jude Elie’s Del Rio statement: what the later investigation qualified
item.description: The agency’s findings describe dangerous conduct while rejecting evidence of people being struck with reins. Both findings belong in the account.

item.title: Tardieu and Deronneth: decide who represents the village before pricing the job
item.description: One historical proposal removes ASEC; another advocates better pay. The comparison needs institutions, dates and responsibilities.

item.title: Tardieu’s 2018 reform: who gets power when legislators stay away?
item.description: Two passages in the commission report offer different answers to the number needed for Parliament to meet.

item.title: Dupuy’s deportation warning: a weekly target is not a weekly count
item.description: The Dominican announcement and Haiti’s reception figure describe different measures over different periods.

item.title: Dupuy’s international network: the links the record actually shows
item.description: A fellowship list and an institutional photograph establish participation. The next reporting questions concern purpose, funding and commitments.

item.title: Deronneth’s local-pay proposal needs a monthly revenue story
item.description: Better pay deserves debate. Historical fund allegations and future payroll obligations require different accounts.

item.title: Deronneth’s equal departmental grant buys unequal amounts per resident
item.description: A population-based calculation reveals the choice hidden inside an apparently equal split.

item.title: Deronneth’s budget: the number beneath the division sign
item.description: His posted amounts can be reproduced. Changing the number of eligible territories changes the cheque each would receive.

item.title: Tardieu’s library promise should be judged from a reader’s chair
item.description: Putting books on a computer can help. The public service begins when a young reader can actually use them.

item.title: Tardieu in Aquin: follow the equipment beyond the donation photograph
item.description: A named hospital gives the aid claim a place to investigate. It does not yet give the public a delivery or patient-use record.

item.title: Tardieu’s UCREF vote: who should control the money investigators?
item.description: His account celebrated a bill. A rights organisation warned about independence. The missing legislative chain matters to both claims.

item.title: The votes behind Tardieu’s terrorist-financing announcement
item.description: A transmission letter separates the first chamber’s vote, the Senate’s vote and publication of the law.

item.title: Tardieu and the Paris Agreement: three dates, three different steps
item.description: A parliamentary announcement and an international ratification notice can both be accurate without describing the same event.

item.title: Martelly’s Cap-Haïtien flight: what was new, and what came before
item.description: The airline’s own announcement identifies a particular route. It also reminds readers that the company had served Haiti for decades.

item.title: Martelly’s 5,000 seats: a public number with two different meanings
item.description: The inauguration account separated 4,000 seats from 1,000 standing places. The distinction changes what citizens can check.

item.title: Hans Joseph’s SEL: count the path from investigation to justice
item.description: Security, the rule of law and fighting corruption are clear priorities. Citizens need to see how results would be measured.

item.title: Barrau’s 800 patients: what a clinic photograph cannot count
item.description: His own caption recognises the limits of mobile care. Patient totals and funding need a different kind of evidence.

item.title: Deronneth and the council: rejection, qualified support, congratulations
item.description: Three dated messages show a change in public positioning. They do not explain a private motive.

item.title: Deronneth’s symposium trail: the cancellation belongs beside the invitation
item.description: A later notice changes what the earlier publicity can prove. Other meetings cannot silently replace the cancelled event.

item.title: Dupuy’s 33 women: the same announcement, two different tenses
item.description: The Creole text promises promotions; the French says they happened. Appointment records would resolve the timing.

item.title: Dupuy’s six reform texts: the distance between submitting and changing the rules
item.description: Her own August 2024 wording describes possible cabinet adoption. That qualification matters when judging a governing record.

item.title: Dupuy announced 400 police trainees. Brazil’s records show a first group of 30.
item.description: The documents establish a start, explain a narrower first phase and leave the full outcome unresolved.

item.title: Lumarque’s scholarship promise needs rules that outlive a benefactor
item.description: Personal educational help can change a life. A national policy must explain who qualifies, who pays and how selection stays fair.

item.title: Lumarque, Quisqueya and the fifty learners between two totals
item.description: An encouraging student story leads to a simple arithmetic check—and a larger question about measuring results.

item.title: Jacky Lumarque’s 47 deaths a day: what the linked report actually counted
item.description: A July 2022 comparison loses a crucial distinction between deaths and injuries. The horror needs no inflated category.

item.title: Etzer Emile: 41 files and a promise for his first 100 days
item.description: He promises resources for existing justice units. BINUH’s record provides a baseline for examining that pledge.

item.title: Etzer Emile vs Gandhy Dorfeuille: from capacity to electricity at home
item.description: A national target and a local launch require different service measures. Insecurity adds a continuity question.

item.title: Tardieu and Barrau: two youth programmes, different missions
item.description: A proposed national guard and a civic-service corps are different institutions. Compare missions, command and participants’ rights first.

item.title: Hans Joseph vs Muscadin: an investigation needs a verifiable outcome
item.description: Corruption files and security-abuse allegations remain separate. Both require knowing what follows a case opening.

item.title: Opinion: protecting a power plant belongs in the electricity promise
item.description: Building, connecting and protecting are three tasks. Energy projects should explain continuing service after launch.

item.title: Opinion: a quiet neighbourhood is not proof of freedom
item.description: Election security should assess whether people can speak and resist coercion, including places with few reported incidents.

item.title: Opinion: a report’s date is not always the date of violence
item.description: Accurate data help protect survivors. Mixing dates can make political debate describe a false change in security.

item.title: Olivier Barrau: at 16, what protection would the youth corps provide?
item.description: The proposal includes minors. Schooling, work, consent and protection need rules, without conflating civic service with an armed force.

item.title: Déus Deronneth: election security begins before polling day
item.description: Reported gang-imposed candidate lists show why freedom of choice goes beyond being able to reach a polling station.

item.title: Muscadin: after arrest, what justice awaits?
item.description: Prison data put trials, care and detention inside the security debate. Arrest is not a verdict.

item.title: Etzer Emile: recruiting more police requires follow-up on existing cases
item.description: An internal-investigation record distinguishes opening a case, completing it and making its outcome available.

item.title: Munir Mourra vs Joanas Gué: credit needs a harvest that can reach a market
item.description: A proposed agricultural bank and a past canal-repair account connect finance, water and maintenance in one policy question.

item.title: Olivier Barrau vs Wilson Jeudy: what kind of money does the figure measure?
item.description: A company balance sheet and a municipal cash statement are not two measures of the candidates’ personal wealth.

item.title: Dominique Dupuy vs Michelet Nestor: from a letter to protection
item.description: A candidate’s 2015 letter and a minister’s 2024 assignment call for different scrutiny of authority, follow-up and results.

item.title: Opinion: a consultation needs a route to follow
item.description: We support following the care pathway: where patients go next, what they pay and who follows up.

item.title: Opinion: count women, then examine the positions
item.description: An overall percentage can hide principal–deputy differences. Making them visible gives the debate a fairer foundation.

item.title: Opinion: a public machine needs more than a photograph
item.description: We want inventories connecting payments, equipment and service. That protects public money without convicting anyone from a photograph.

item.title: Joanas Gué: when school closes, what happens to the child’s meal?
item.description: Local buying can support farmers and children. School closures show why meal totals do not answer every access question.

item.title: Munir Mourra: before a new centre, where is the water?
item.description: A family-cistern project shows why even small infrastructure needs maintenance, sharing rules and service checks.

item.title: Etzer Emile: how long would 50,000 temporary jobs last?
item.description: People employed and days worked are different measures. A simple example shows why duration changes the promise’s cost and value.

item.title: Privert and the Neptune record: another step in 2007
item.description: The inter-American judgment quotes a decision after the 2006 release. Its jurisdiction discussion is not a collective verdict.

item.title: Claude Joseph vs Jocelerme Privert: temporary power and deadlines
item.description: An acting premier in 2021 and a provisional president in 2016 held different offices. Both records raise questions about handing over power.

item.title: Munir Mourra vs Jude Elie: when private-sector experience seeks state power
item.description: Partnership proposals and construction interests require clear separation between experience and personal benefit.

item.title: Etzer Emile vs Jude Elie: infrastructure promises and planning experience
item.description: A national programme and a NYCHA role are different evidence. Costs, maintenance and responsibility connect their assessment.

item.title: Walsonn Sanon vs Michelet Nestor: whose consent counts?
item.description: Rejecting an agreement and winning a nomination measure different things. Both invite clear rules on who participated.

item.title: Hans Joseph vs Kely Bastien: transparency should leave a record
item.description: One led ULCC, the other the Senate. Their experience calls for different records to assess what they did.

item.title: Martine Moïse vs Jocelerme Privert: two decisions with different effects
item.description: Restarting an inquiry and releasing a person are different decisions. Neither automatically decides the substance of the allegations.

item.title: Opinion: the food crisis needs two campaign calendars
item.description: We should assess what feeds a household now alongside what improves its livelihood over several years.

item.title: Joanas Gué: the next president will not start agriculture from zero
item.description: PARSA already has funding, activities and reported weaknesses. They belong in scrutiny of a former agriculture minister.

item.title: Etzer Emile: 2033 jobs and a trade window ending in 2028
item.description: The industrial programme runs beyond the HOPE/HELP extension. That calls for a plan for the years after 2028.

item.title: Jovenel Moïse’s assassination: the trail of a US$175,000 loan
item.description: The Miami trial summary describes pandemic-relief proceeds entering the plot’s financing. The trail requires specific people and accounts.

item.title: Wilson Jeudy vs Savannah Savary: employee numbers do not establish capacity to pay wages
item.description: A mayor’s statement on municipal cash and an entrepreneur’s employment account require separating available funds, costs and job totals.

item.title: Jude Elie vs Olivier Barrau: a company name is not an asset declaration
item.description: Entrepreneurial biographies, partner titles and a company balance sheet supply different information. Comparing them requires preserving each document’s limits.

item.title: Kely Bastien vs Clarens Renois: leaders’ agreement is not every citizen’s mandate
item.description: DELIVRANS nomination and 2015 Protestant negotiations require understanding who could commit whom.

item.title: Gary Bodeau vs Jocelerme Privert: a vote count is not the entire story of selecting a leader
item.description: A 2016 National Assembly vote and U.S. allegations concerning 2018–2019 appointments are different records of parliamentary power.

item.title: Savannah Savary vs Martine Moïse: who else do their parties present to voters?
item.description: A woman presidential registrant does not explain the composition of all her party’s registrations. The CEP snapshot provides a bounded starting point.

item.title: Women in the candidate registry: a 30.6% total can conceal positions with fewer women
item.description: We counted 11,142 CEP rows by reported sex, office and position. Principal and deputy mayoral positions present different pictures.

item.title: Olivier Barrau and ten-dollar insurance: a premium is not the whole cost of care
item.description: AIC supplies a 2022 price indicator for part of its clientele. It guarantees neither free care nor a current price for every family.

item.title: Olivier Barrau: what AIC owns and what it owes
item.description: The 2022 balance sheet separates what the company holds, owes and retains for shareholders. It is not the candidate’s personal wealth.

item.title: Jocelerme Privert: three pages explaining the limits of his 2006 release
item.description: The Gonaïves decision grants release subject to appearance. It also says the application does not open a merits examination.

item.title: Hans Joseph and Badio: what the May 2021 employment record establishes
item.description: An ULCC statement put employment, departure and complaint dates on record. It does not turn past employment into proof of conspiracy.

item.title: Savannah Savary vs Jacky Lumarque: what remains after an activity about rights?
item.description: Savary’s writing workshops and a research library presented by Lumarque offer different resources to examine without treating an activity as a national outcome.

item.title: Claude Joseph vs Gary Bodeau: two foreign lists do not mean the same decision
item.description: An entry restriction and financial sanctions require separating the authority, measure, grounds and the person’s response.

item.title: Wilson Jeudy vs René St-Fort: a displaced family should not disappear from public services
item.description: The 2011 Delmas evictions and 2026 electoral access are distinct records. Both raise how authorities remain accountable to people losing their place of residence.

item.title: Kely Bastien vs Jocelerme Privert: when provisional power reaches its deadline
item.description: A 2010 position and a 120-day mandate in 2016 raise a shared question: who decides after the deadline?

item.title: Joanas Gué vs Olivier Barrau: a harvest can be good while its market is closed
item.description: Mangoes barred from export and rainfall-triggered insurance concern different risks within farming life.

item.title: Munir Mourra vs Jerry Tardieu: partnership does not always mean the same contract
item.description: MPH’s proposed farm-distribution centres and Royal Oasis financing require separating loans, equity and state responsibility.

item.title: Gandhy Dorfeuille vs Munir Mourra: construction schedules differ from the hours electricity arrives
item.description: Saint-Louis du Sud in 2014 and a Jacmel record in 2026 provide two ways to examine an energy promise’s results.

item.title: Martine Moïse vs Dominique Dupuy: representing Haiti does not explain every power of an office
item.description: A 2018 health-coordination role and a 2024 ministry require separating public appearances, decisions and accountability.

item.title: Opinion: an agricultural bank must change where credit reaches
item.description: BRH reports 75.64% of credit in Ouest for one quarter. Rural-finance promises need measures of how lending reaches beyond it.

item.title: Opinion: scrutiny of a contract needs people able to question it without threats
item.description: Dermalog has another documentary trail: protection of those who criticized it. That does not permit inventing the threats’ authors.

item.title: Lucmanne Delille vs Jean Ernest Muscadin: an officer’s rights and limits on power belong together
item.description: A 2020 police-union decision and a 2023 jurisdictional reprimand illuminate two sides of public service.

item.title: Hans Joseph vs Etzer Emile: oversight must be able to examine their own side
item.description: An economist who criticized constraints on the Court of Accounts and a former ULCC director must explain protections for those scrutinizing their own power.

item.title: Savannah Savary vs Jude Elie: who controls the business during a presidential term?
item.description: Inherited firms, declared businesses and a partner title require different records. The public issue is power over decisions affecting those interests.

item.title: Jerry Tardieu vs René St-Fort: speaking with a citizen is not their signature of support
item.description: Constitutional consultation and party membership serve different functions. Both need a record of what the citizen actually agreed to.

item.title: Etzer Emile vs Jacky Lumarque: who checks employment after the diploma?
item.description: Emile links employer-training support to employment entry. Lumarque’s record allows scrutiny of how training outcomes are measured over time.

item.title: Munir Mourra vs Jacky Lumarque: a campus needs a budget after construction
item.description: A proposed campus for at least 4,000 students and a rector’s experience raise questions about fees, teachers and the university’s purpose.

item.title: Munir Mourra: Jacmel’s energy plan already has a construction site to account for
item.description: MPH names Jacmel in diesel-plant rehabilitation. A World Bank report documents a separate solar-and-battery construction project there.

item.title: Etzer Emile and the 40% women’s credit target: whom do we count, what money do we follow?
item.description: A beneficiary target is not automatically a loan-amount target. BRH’s figures require additional distinctions.

item.title: Etzer Emile and bank reserves: 40% is not the rule for every currency
item.description: The programme proposes lower reserves on gourde deposits. A BRH note shows why bank and currency categories must remain clear.

item.title: Etzer Emile and business creation in 48 hours: what is new about one window?
item.description: An MCI portal already exists online. The campaign promise needs to distinguish completing a form from obtaining every document a business needs.

item.title: Martine Moïse and malaria: what became of the 2020 goal?
item.description: In 2018, she backed malaria elimination. Health data for 2025 show the disease persisted. They raise a policy-continuity question without assigning one person all national outcomes.

item.title: Martine Moïse and Dermalog: a signature and influence are different questions
item.description: An identity-card contract, influence allegations and an explicit denial: following the decisions means keeping a complaint distinct from a conviction.

item.title: Jerry Tardieu vs Jude Célestin: after the financing, what assets and services remain?
item.description: A private hotel and public equipment are different records. Both show why financing figures need accounts of what they delivered.

item.title: Jean Ernest Muscadin vs Munir Mourra: an armored vehicle is not a security budget
item.description: Citizens can buy equipment. A state must fund its use, maintenance and oversight for years. Those responsibilities deserve examining together.

item.title: Etzer Emile vs Joanas Gué: buying local means paying producers on time
item.description: Using food purchases to support local production was on the table in 2010. This comparison follows the path from contract to delivery and payment.

item.title: Etzer Emile vs René St-Fort: who makes sure the teacher gets paid?
item.description: A common curriculum and a larger budget can help schools. Money must also reach the teacher, on the date it is due.

item.title: Dominique Dupuy vs Savannah Savary: the same precision, different rules for money
item.description: A diplomatic-spending decision and an account of family businesses are different records. They help identify what the public needs to assess each candidate.

item.title: Clarens Renois vs Junior Salomon: what oversight remains when allies hold power?
item.description: A signature on the 2024 pact and an OPL protest in 2025 show why political accountability needs more than ally or opponent labels.

item.title: Olivier Barrau vs Munir Mourra: an agricultural bank needs an answer when a harvest fails
item.description: Credit, irrigation and insurance belong to the same farming season. They address different problems, but their rules need to work together.

item.title: Jerry Tardieu vs Jacky Lumarque: a scholarship must identify who pays and who selects
item.description: Both attended a 2020 scholarship launch. That connection does not merge the programmes into one fund or make the financing a personal gift.

item.title: Claude Joseph vs Etzer Emile: emergency powers and capacity that must endure
item.description: One headed a cabinet after the president’s assassination. The other proposes expanding police. The comparison follows deadlines, oversight and what lasts after the first announcement.

item.title: Jean Ernest Muscadin vs Michel Martelly: public protection needs answers about power
item.description: A UN report about a prosecutor and U.S. sanctions against a former president are different records. They require distinct evidentiary paths and the same precision.

item.title: Etzer Emile vs Jerry Tardieu: who chooses the road, and who maintains it?
item.description: A large investment plan and a debate over departmental power meet at one question: how does a national decision keep serving a commune?

item.title: Etzer Emile vs Olivier Barrau: after a loss, who carries the cost?
item.description: A loan can start or expand an activity. Insurance can help after a shock. Comparing these records means following risk as well as announced money.

item.title: Michel Martelly vs Etzer Emile: follow school money into the classroom
item.description: A transfer-fee record and two budget targets show why money collected, authorized and spent must remain distinct.

item.title: Martine Moïse vs Claude Joseph: one killing, different judicial roles
item.description: A survivor and a former prime minister appear at different judicial stages. Election registration neither erases those records nor supplies a verdict on them.

item.title: Walsonn Sanon vs Clarens Renois: rejecting one pact, signing another
item.description: The agreements and years differ. Their positions allow scrutiny of participation in transitional decisions and how leaders account for those choices.

item.title: Jude Elie vs Wilner Joseph: an institution’s name does not explain a person’s role
item.description: A NYCHA chart and a report identifying a government adviser provide two starting points. Roles, dates and outcomes need separating before experience can be assessed.

item.title: Gandhy Dorfeuille vs Joanas Gué: after the launch, does the service last?
item.description: Electricity and irrigation are different services. Both require tracing money through completed work to the maintenance people need afterward.

item.title: Déus Deronneth vs Marc-Arthur Drouillard: a result is not the whole election story
item.description: One obtained a changed result after challenges. The other announced withdrawal to support Jovenel Moïse. These are different political acts to examine.

item.title: Kely Bastien vs Junior Salomon: a Senate title does not explain all the power
item.description: Their records raise different questions: how a leader accounts for his decisions, and how he obtains authority to lead.

item.title: Daniest Adrien vs Ricardo Jean Pierre: a party slate is not its vote total
item.description: PRC has more Senate entries; PANAH has one more deputy entry. The data show participation in the contest without predicting who will win.

item.title: Martine Moïse joins the list: 33 presidential registrations
item.description: Three women appear in the late November 15 reading. Registration opens a record to examine; it is neither final approval nor a measure of election chances.

item.title: Savannah Savary vs Olivier Barrau: family businesses and the public interest
item.description: Their business histories explain part of their careers. The public question concerns what they control today and the safeguards they accept for tomorrow.

item.title: Wilson Jeudy vs Jude Célestin: public works must account for the people affected
item.description: Delmas camp clearances and CNE equipment purchases are different records. They offer two ways to examine authority, resources and public service.

item.title: Hans Joseph vs Lucmanne Delille: an investigation must reach a judge
item.description: A former ULCC head and a former justice minister held different responsibilities. Their records direct attention to the full justice process, beyond an investigation’s announcement.

item.title: Jacky Lumarque vs René St-Fort: from the lesson to a student’s life
item.description: Training experience and proposals on teachers’ conditions address different parts of the same chain. Access, learning and what follows all need examination.

item.title: Etzer Emile vs Munir Mourra: doubling police is not doubling budgets
item.description: Two security proposals use doubling. One counts people; the other counts money. The outcome for citizens requires more than those figures.

item.title: Etzer Emile vs Moïse Durocher: what counts as a job?
item.description: A small-business loan, temporary employment and a lasting job are different outcomes. Campaign totals need common definitions before comparison.

item.title: Clarens Renois vs Maxo Joseph: a church agreement does not own anyone’s vote
item.description: They participated in the same political process in 2015. Later records show why alliances need dates and support networks must be distinguished from voters’ rights.

item.title: Jerry Tardieu vs Gary Bodeau: who controlled access in Parliament?
item.description: The 2019 record raises access to documents. U.S. sanctions against Bodeau raise a separate question about money and influence that must remain distinct.

item.title: Dominique Dupuy vs Claude Joseph: after diplomatic words, what protection?
item.description: The former foreign ministers bring different records at the same border. A public stance alone does not measure what changed for citizens.

item.title: Michel Martelly vs Jocelerme Privert: two presidents, different accountability tests
item.description: Martelly’s school promise and Privert’s transitional mandate are different records. Comparing them requires separating money, authority and deadlines.

item.title: Jerry Tardieu vs Olivier Barrau: business experience must show whom it serves
item.description: A hotel and an insurer received international financing. Comparing the records means following the money to the people it was intended to help.

item.title: Etzer Emile vs Jean Ernest Muscadin: more police, accountable to whom?
item.description: One offers police recruitment targets. The other has a prosecutorial record that raises questions about the use of force. Security requires examining both.

item.title: After parties choose, public debate should begin
item.description: Our view: nomination should open a programme to public scrutiny rather than close questions inside an organization.

item.title: An institution-funded scholarship should remain a civic opportunity
item.description: Our view: crediting someone who opens a door should never create a political obligation for the recipient.

item.title: Security should give citizens protection they can trust
item.description: Our view: anger at gang violence requires a state response that protects life and answers for its own use of force.

item.title: When examining a candidate’s family, follow the exercise of power
item.description: Our view: inheritance, appointments and business interests merit precise scrutiny. Kinship does not establish guilt.

item.title: A transition needs an exit beyond its leader’s discretion
item.description: Our view: security conditions need public measures, and temporary mandates need enforceable limits.

item.title: Public money, private money: candidates should make the distinction visible
item.description: Our view: a popular name or compelling story should not replace financial records that allow citizens to scrutinize power.

item.title: Before Martine Moïse’s entry: Dupuy and Savary in the 32-name list
item.description: The earlier November 15 reading had two entries coded F among 32. Martine Moïse’s later entry brought the list to 33, with three coded F. These are two points in a changing registry.

item.title: Lucmanne Delille: a signature on police officers’ right to organize
item.description: The March 2020 order supplies a concrete measure in his ministerial record. Signing a text and securing its implementation are connected tasks.

item.title: The decree Hans Joseph criticized: which gate must a case pass?
item.description: The December 2025 text places a parliamentary step in the prosecution of certain senior officials. Its own preamble acknowledges an inoperative legislature.

item.title: Martelly’s asset disclosures: why 20 plus 17 does not automatically mean 37
item.description: ULCC’s allegations require precise scrutiny. Accounts counted at different times are not necessarily different accounts.

item.title: Jerry Tardieu and French scholarships: who financed the opportunity?
item.description: A deputy’s role in assembling partners deserves recognition. Institutional funding and work also need to remain visible.

item.title: Wilner Joseph: from advising government to competing for office
item.description: Government relationships need documentation. They establish neither control of government nor a reason to ignore electoral fairness.

item.title: Claude Joseph, EDE and Smith Augustin: what responsibility does a party carry?
item.description: A party defended its representative, then sought his resignation. The sequence invites scrutiny of political decisions without transferring criminal allegations between people.

item.title: Martelly in the Moïse inquiry in July 2026: testimony is not conviction
item.description: A judicial appearance is a specific event. It should be kept distinct from other allegations or sanctions concerning the former president.

item.title: Claude Joseph: what the 2022 Dominican entry ban establishes
item.description: His name appeared in an instruction containing other names. That alone does not establish a criminal relationship among them.

item.title: Michelet Nestor in 2015: defending people of Haitian descent beyond a slogan
item.description: His letter to Danilo Medina records a concrete demand. It also highlights the distinction between a person’s ancestry and legal status.

item.title: Deus Deronneth in 2024: challenging a council is not annulling it
item.description: He invoked sovereignty and separation of powers. Understanding the position requires distinguishing a candidate’s argument from a judicial decision.

item.title: Salomon and OPL: opposing a council that included another party leader
item.description: A 2025 protest in Les Cayes shows why a party does not always speak with one voice. Connections and disagreements both need documenting.

item.title: Joanas Gué and mango exports in 2007: reopening did not end the crisis
item.description: An announced mid-July restart was followed by another suspension at month-end. Following the dates changes the assessment.

item.title: Joanas Gué after the 2008 storms: losses are not recovery funding
item.description: Damage estimates, recovery plans and budget funding are separate stages. Combining them makes a public response harder to assess.

item.title: Jacky Lumarque and Mouka: a public resource behind the speech
item.description: A 2023 address on women’s rights points to a verifiable institutional action. It offers a way to examine the record of a rector seeking office.

item.title: Dominique Dupuy: after condemning deportations, what protection followed?
item.description: A 2024 official communiqué records the diplomatic task assigned to her. Assessing the record requires following what happened to the people affected.

item.title: René St-Fort: displacement should not erase a vote
item.description: His registration position highlights an easily missed barrier: an office can remain open while the citizen cannot reach it.

item.title: Nestor, Savary and DPA: a launch did not settle every affiliation
item.description: Dated records show why appearing at a political event does not, by itself, establish someone’s eventual party affiliation.

item.title: Michelet Nestor: modest origins, big promises and the record
item.description: A 2015 profile records the social story accompanying his political entry. A life story provides context; it does not replace evidence of management.

item.title: Deus Deronneth: waiting for security, but until when?
item.description: His criticism of changing electoral rules raises a real difficulty: protecting voters while keeping the transition time-bound.

item.title: Hans Joseph: leaving ULCC and claiming independence
item.description: The former director offers an explanation for his dismissal. His account and a proven motive are different things.

item.title: René St-Fort and 30,000 supporters: a citizen’s name is not a blank signature
item.description: PRN’s challenge opens a debate about consent. Enabling verification need not expose everyone’s political choices.

item.title: René St-Fort: a common curriculum needs the means to teach it
item.description: His education proposals connect two issues: what children should learn and the conditions of those who teach them.

item.title: Wilson Jeudy in 2016: four million in cash, more than 18 million in payroll
item.description: A simple comparison explains the problem he described. It does not establish responsibility or trace every gourde.

item.title: Jerry Tardieu and governors: autonomy still needs accountability
item.description: The 2025 dispute reaches beyond the word “federal.” It concerns who manages departmental money and who can demand accounts.

item.title: Claude Joseph in July 2021: emergency power and a handover
item.description: After Jovenel Moïse’s assassination, executive authority became an immediate question. Following the sequence allows scrutiny of Joseph’s political record without conflating it with the criminal case.

item.title: Tardieu and Bodeau in 2019: the records, the vote and what it did not settle
item.description: A debate over impeaching Jovenel Moïse ended in a disputed vote. Its political outcome did not adjudicate every financial allegation.

item.title: Jude Célestin: from boycott to a new election
item.description: Challenging an election, obtaining a rerun and winning it are different outcomes. The 2015–2016 crisis illustrates the distinction.
